**The configuration reference is now generated.** The whole env-var surface in [the configuration reference](https://pvliesdonk.github.io/markdown-vault-mcp/unstable/reference/configuration/index.md) is produced from the config model itself and guarded in CI, so the tables can no longer drift from the code. One correction rode along: the JWT signing key documentation had claimed the key was required on Linux/Docker because the default was ephemeral; in fact the default is derived from the client secret and survives restarts ([#1247](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1247)).

**Attachment extensions now accept the spellings people write.** An operator who set `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_ATTACHMENT_EXTENSIONS=PDF` or `.pdf` got an allowlist that matched nothing, with every attachment refused by an error message listing the extensions they had just configured ([#1239](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1239), [#1280](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1280)). Case and a leading dot are now ignored, so `PDF`, `.pdf`, and `pdf` name the same type. This only widens what is accepted; no working configuration changes meaning. Library callers passing `attachment_extensions=` get the same normalization.

**The git guide now says what the remote must permit.** It documented which credentials to configure but not what the token had to be allowed to do, so two ordinary first-run conditions each cost a long detour before the real git error was found: a protected default branch that refused the push, and a clone with no usable token, whose fetches failed ([#1337](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1337)). The managed-git section now states both prerequisites (push access to the tracked branch, and a branch protection that refuses regardless of the token's scopes) and points at `git_sync(direction="push")` as the call that returns the remote's own refusal message, with a note on why `git push --dry-run` is not a substitute for it.

## For library consumers

`Vault` construction is now settings-first: a `VaultSettings` object (importable from `markdown_vault_mcp.vault` alongside `Vault`) replaces what had grown into "a flattened config bus" of 35 keyword parameters ([#1158](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1158), [#1224](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1224)). Every legacy keyword still works. Deprecation is docstring-only, with removal scheduled for the next major, but mixing `settings=` with a non-default legacy keyword raises `ValueError` naming each conflict: pick one mode per construction. Collaborator arguments (`embedding_provider`, `summarizer`, `git_strategy`, `on_write`, `chunk_strategy`) and `source_dir` stay as keywords and are not deprecated. See the [Vault API page](https://pvliesdonk.github.io/markdown-vault-mcp/unstable/reference/api/vault/index.md).

Under the hood, the concrete classes now sit behind protocols: `git_strategy` is typed against a `VersionedStore` protocol rather than the concrete `GitWriteStrategy`, and `markdown_vault_mcp.git` and `markdown_vault_mcp.interfaces` export the protocol names. A consumer who passes a `GitWriteStrategy` needs to do nothing; the type only widened ([#1237](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1237)). The protocols are documented in the design notes rather than the API reference.

One inherited behavior note from [fastmcp-pvl-core 6](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/fastmcp-pvl-core/releases/tag/v6.0.0): `make_server()` now finalizes instructions synchronously and must not be called from a running event loop.

## Upgrading

**No breaking changes.** No env var, tool, or importable name changes meaning; the operator surface only grew (two GitLab webhook variables, `INSTANCE_DESCRIPTION`). A few things do change behavior without any action on your part:

- **The text index rebuilds once on first start.** Seven changes in this release alter how stored rows derive from a note's bytes: skip tombstones ([#1227](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1227)), any-scheme external links ([#1335](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1335)), percent-decoded destinations ([#1332](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1332)), attachment references leaving the link graph ([#1333](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1333)), links bounded to one paragraph ([#1334](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1334)), destinations read in every CommonMark spelling ([#1353](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1353)), and the wikilink tie-break observed on Obsidian ([#1350](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1350)). `INDEX_SEMANTICS_VERSION` moved from 2 to 9 (the values between never shipped; a vault on 4.2.0-rc.0 holds 3 and rebuilds once more). One rebuild covers all seven; it is automatic, costs CPU and local IO proportional to vault size, and does not re-embed. Expect the link graph to change on it: `get_broken_links` and `stats.broken_link_count` drop (attachment embeds, schemed URLs and stray-bracket prose leave, encoded and CommonMark-spelled links now resolve), `get_orphan_notes` and `stats.orphan_count` can gain notes whose only links were embeds, and in a vault with duplicate note names a bare `[[Note]]` can re-point to the note beside it, as it does in Obsidian.
- **A note becomes stale one day earlier, and an instant is honoured.** `stale_after` is now the first stale day rather than the last current one ([#1357](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1357)), so a note dated today flips to `stale: true` on upgrade; a note whose `stale_after` was a quoted instant (`'2026-01-01T00:00:00Z'`), which the server used to ignore, is now stale when that instant has passed ([#1373](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1373)). Triage listings built with `{"stale": "true"}` may gain entries, and may lose one for a note whose `stale_after` carried a time but no offset (previously read as its date, now ignored). No stored rows change, so no rebuild.
- **`generated.at` moves on every content write.** It is now the UTC instant of the write rather than the date ([#1372](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1372)), so a rewrite of unchanged content, which used to leave the file byte-identical when the same actor wrote it on the same day, now changes the stamp and, on a git-backed vault, produces a commit. Stamps already on disk stay bare dates until the note is next written.
- **A vault whose root `index.md` starts with a byte-order mark becomes an OKF bundle on upgrade** ([#1407](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1407)). Its declaration was invisible before, so results gain OKF annotations, the OKF filters start matching, and reserved files and deprecated or stale notes take their ranking downweights. Because `type`, `status` and `stale_after` join the structured-filter set on an active bundle, that vault also rebuilds its index once, on the existing `indexed_frontmatter_fields` provenance check rather than a semantics bump. Nothing on disk changes.
- **`okf_validate` can report index files it used to pass.** A vault with `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_REQUIRED_FIELDS` set sees each `index.md` the server wrote those fields into under the new `index_frontmatter` finding ([#1396](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1396)). Nothing is re-indexed or rewritten; do not remove the required fields, or the index drops out of search.
- **Two `fix(release)` entries in the changelog** ([#1327](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1327), [#1329](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1329)) are repairs to the release pipeline itself, with no runtime effect.
- **A Voyage vault also re-embeds once**, through a separate mechanism with a separate trigger: the provider's embedding behavior is part of the vector sidecar's identity, and asymmetric embedding changed it ([#1270](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1270)). This one costs Voyage API calls. Vaults on other providers load warm.
- **A note that fails to parse stops serving its last-good content.** It drops from search and read until fixed, and is listed in `get_index_status.skipped_files`.
- **Bulk calls produce one commit.** Tooling that expected one commit per file from `okf_convert_links`, `move_folder`, or link-updating `rename` now sees `<tool>: N files`. Single-file writes keep their old subjects.
- **On OIDC deployments with commit claims configured, commit authorship changes**, from the static fallback identity to the authenticated user, which is what the configuration always promised.
- **A stdio deployment with a webhook credential starts its file watcher** where it previously ran nothing, and logs that the credential is inert on that transport.
- **If your `INSTRUCTIONS_EXTRA` describes what the vault contains**, move that part to `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_INSTANCE_DESCRIPTION`; keep rules of behavior where they are. Long instruction text now logs a budget warning at startup rather than being silently cut by the client.
- **Fresh package installs get a fully commented `env.example`**; every assignment now documents a default instead of setting one. A deployed `/etc/markdown-vault-mcp/env` is never overwritten.

This release is not the FastMCP 4 move: the template's v8 line and fastmcp-pvl-core 7 carry that migration, tracked for the next major as [#1271](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1271).

# 5.0

5.0 is a major release, and most deployments have something to change. The server moves to FastMCP 4. Compose publishes on loopback without a proxy, and logs default to JSON off a terminal. Writable servers refuse a blind overwrite of an existing file unless the operator opts out. Python consumers configure `Vault` through `VaultSettings`. Every tool call now ends one of four ways: done, change the request, refresh and retry, or a server fault. Refusals log at INFO with a next step; only real faults log at ERROR with a traceback. Links the server writes work in Obsidian, the link graph picks up link forms it used to miss, and large vaults no longer pay a full-table scan per changed note. The index follows git HEAD, so notes deleted by a pull leave the listings. OKF stops treating a bearer credential as a person and keeps its generated `index.md` listings current. Read [Upgrading](#upgrading) before you move.

This is the first stable release since [4.2](https://pvliesdonk.github.io/markdown-vault-mcp/unstable/releases/4.2/index.md). One outside report shaped it: a 25,380-note vault whose reindex read over a terabyte from disk. Two threads run through the rest. Breaking changes announced during 4.x now land: overwrite protection on by default, the `VaultSettings`-only constructor, the claim arguments removed. And the server now reports what happened truthfully to whoever asks, whether that is a model calling a tool, an operator reading the log, or Python code catching an exception.

## Upgrading

Before moving a 4.2 deployment or integration to 5.0:

1. **Compose:** set `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SOURCE_DIR` in `.env` to the vault's directory on the host. Move proxy labels and networks into an override. Without a proxy the server is reachable only on `127.0.0.1:8000`; to serve other machines, configure authentication and publish from the override.
1. **Container port:** if you set `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_PORT` for the image, remove it and change the host side of the port mapping instead.
1. **Overwrites:** decide whether writes may still replace existing files blindly. The default now refuses them; set `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_WRITE_PROTECT_EXISTING=false` only where you need the old behaviour.
1. **Logging:** replace `FASTMCP_LOG_LEVEL` with `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_LOG_LEVEL`, remove `FASTMCP_ENABLE_RICH_LOGGING`, and set `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_LOG_FORMAT=rich` wherever you want coloured output off a terminal. Update log queries and alerts: messages use the `event_name key=value` form, and tool refusals are INFO, not ERROR.
1. **Authentication:** if `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_AUTH_MODE` is set, make sure the variables its mode requires are set too.
1. **OKF review over bearer tokens:** switch `trust-auth` to `elicit` with a client that shows the confirmation to a person.
1. **Python:** move FastMCP 3 environments to FastMCP 4; move `Vault` keywords into `VaultSettings` and replace `to_vault_kwargs`; remove the two claim arguments from `GitWriteStrategy`; add `set_commit_observer` and `start(on_tick)` to any custom `git_strategy`; handle `DocumentUnreadableError` from `read()` and `read_revision()`; and handle the refusals from `get_similar` and `list_tags` where you relied on `[]`.
1. **Vault directory:** the server no longer refuses to start when its own `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SOURCE_DIR` is unset or missing (Compose still needs the `.env` value from step 1). Watch for `vault_directory_missing` in the log if you relied on the refusal.

**Clients:** nothing to do beyond reconnecting. The tool set is unchanged, and a client picks up the new tool descriptions when it reconnects after the restart.

**State:** kept. Under Compose, the index, the embeddings and the OIDC state stay on the `state-data` volume at `/data/state`, and no volume moves; the new `service-data` volume stays empty. The first start rebuilds the text index once, because 5.0 changes how its rows are derived from the notes. The embeddings survive it: only a note whose sections came out different from that rebuild is embedded again. On a large vault that restarts often, consider `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_BOOT_REINDEX=false`.

**Security posture:** narrower in three ways and wider in one. Compose publishes on `127.0.0.1` only; a whole-file `write` or `fetch` onto an existing file needs that file's etag; and a bearer credential no longer counts as a person for OKF review. HTTP deployments gain the unauthenticated `/health` and `/health/ready` routes, whose bodies `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_HEALTH_DETAIL` limits.

## How a tool call ends

In 4.2, the server's own refusals reached FastMCP as unhandled exceptions, so an ordinary refusal was logged at ERROR with a full traceback. A `write` without `if_match`, an `edit` with a stale etag and a `get_outlinks` on a missing path all looked like crashes in the log ([#1608](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1608)). An operator could not alert on ERROR without being paged for a model's typo.

Every tool call now ends in one of four outcomes: the contract was met; the caller must change the request; the caller must refresh, then retry; or the server failed ([#1615](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1615), [#1641](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1641)). What each party sees:

- **In the log**, a refusal is one line at INFO; a busy or still-building index is one line at WARNING. A server fault is logged once, as `tool_failed`, at ERROR with its traceback. Alerting on ERROR now means something broke. Log queries that matched `tool_call_failed` at ERROR for refusals need updating.
- **The model** gets a refusal message that names its next step: which tool to call or what to pass instead ([#1643](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1643)). Refusals no longer name `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_*` settings the model cannot change; the setting goes to the log as a `setting=` field instead. For a fault, the model gets a fixed message saying "the request itself was fine; retry later, and tell the user if it keeps failing" ([fastmcp-pvl-core#374](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/fastmcp-pvl-core/pull/374)). Git's stderr, which carries server paths, no longer reaches the model ([#1632](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1632)).
- **Python code** gets a typed exception; see [the library section](#the-python-library).

The classification also corrected several outcomes that were misreported:

- `get_similar` and the `similar://` resource refuse on a vault without embeddings, and `list_tags` and `tags://` refuse a field that is not indexed. In 4.2 all four returned an empty list, which a model could not tell apart from "no matches" ([#1599](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1599), [#1652](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1652)).
- `summarize` reports notes it skipped in a new `skipped` list, each entry a path and a reason: `not_found`, `invalid_path`, `over_read_limit` or `unreadable`. `notes_omitted` now counts only notes dropped by the note limit; 4.2 blamed unreadable notes on the limit too ([#1637](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1637), [#1644](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1644)).
- A note that exists but cannot be read is a fault, not a missing note. Before this, OKF upkeep could overwrite an unreadable `index.md` or `log.md` as if it were absent ([#1627](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1627)). On Python 3.14, where `pathlib`'s existence checks swallow permission errors, the server now decides existence with `stat()`. An unreadable note is no longer purged from the index, and an unreadable embeddings store no longer triggers a cold rebuild over it ([#1625](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1625), [#1645](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1645), [#1646](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1646)).
- A missing attachment is told apart from a refused read, and a transfer download answers 410 Gone only for a file that is truly gone ([#1638](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1638)).
- `get_diff` with an unknown commit is a refusal, not a git failure ([#1632](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1632)), and `read` with a bad `revision` is a refusal pointing at `get_history` ([#1635](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1635)). A git vault with no commits yet returns an empty history.
- A path holding a NUL byte is a bad request, not a server fault ([#1636](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1636), [#1642](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1642)).

The tool, parameter and resource descriptions were rewritten to state each tool's contract and nothing else. Measured in UTF-16 units, tool descriptions went from 22,930 to 7,971 and input schemas from 28,128 to 21,778 ([#1652](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1652)). The tool set itself is unchanged. The [tools reference](https://pvliesdonk.github.io/markdown-vault-mcp/unstable/reference/tools/index.md) and [resources reference](https://pvliesdonk.github.io/markdown-vault-mcp/unstable/reference/resources/index.md) describe each refusal.

## Overwrite protection is on by default

`MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_WRITE_PROTECT_EXISTING` now defaults to `true`. A whole-file `write` or a `fetch` onto an existing path is refused unless it carries `if_match` set to the target's current etag. `edit`, `append`, `delete` and `rename` are unaffected. The failure being guarded is a model calling `write` where it meant `edit`, and the issue that flipped the default notes that "a default-off guard only protects operators who already know the failure exists, which is the population least likely to hit it" ([#1136](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1136), [#1477](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1477)).

Deliberate replacement still works: `read` the note, then `write` with its etag as `if_match`. An upload link has no `if_match`, so under protection `create_upload_link` refuses an existing destination. To keep 4.2's blind overwrites, set `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_WRITE_PROTECT_EXISTING=false`. The library default in `VaultSettings` stays `False`; the flip is in the server configuration. See [Configuration](https://pvliesdonk.github.io/markdown-vault-mcp/unstable/reference/configuration/index.md).

Two related tool fixes. The `edit` and `rename` descriptions now say when to omit `if_match`: for several text-matching edits to one file at once, and for renaming several linked notes together ([#1493](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1493), [#1572](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1572)). A line-range `edit` with an empty `new_text` deletes the lines; 4.2 left a blank line behind ([#1607](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1607), [#1613](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1613)).

## Running the server

The server moves from FastMCP 3.4.7 to 4.0.10, through `fastmcp-pvl-core` 10 and the fastmcp-server-template 10.2 release ([#1271](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1271), [#1465](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1465), [#1550](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1550), [#1641](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1641), [#1649](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1649)). Most of what an operator notices comes through those upstreams.

### Containers

`compose.yml` no longer assumes Traefik. It pulls the published image instead of building, reads `.env` only if one exists, and publishes port 8000 on `127.0.0.1` because the quick start has no authentication. A health check probes `/health`. The file also mounts a `service-data` volume at `/data/service`, which this server doesn't use: its index, embeddings and OIDC state stay on `state-data` at `/data/state`, as in 4.2. In `.env`, `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SOURCE_DIR` names the vault's directory on the host, which Compose bind-mounts at `/data/vault`, so it must be set; inside the container the file sets the server's own value to `/data/vault` ([#1465](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1465), [#1614](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1614)). To reach the server from other machines, configure authentication first, then use a reverse proxy or publish on every interface from `compose.override.yml`. The [Docker guide](https://pvliesdonk.github.io/markdown-vault-mcp/unstable/deploy/docker/index.md) has the override, and the new [security model](https://pvliesdonk.github.io/markdown-vault-mcp/unstable/security-model/index.md) page explains what the loopback bind does and does not protect.

The image pins its listener to port 8000 and adds a `HEALTHCHECK`. In 4.2, `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_PORT` moved the container's listener; it no longer does. To serve on another host port, change the host side of the port mapping (`"127.0.0.1:9000:8000"`) ([#1465](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1465)).

### Health and shutdown

HTTP deployments gain unauthenticated `/health` (liveness) and `/health/ready` (503 when a readiness check fails) routes, placed beside the MCP mount path. `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_HEALTH_DETAIL` sets how much the bodies reveal: `status`, `standard` (the default, which adds name, version and per-check verdicts) or `full` (adds redacted reasons; for trusted networks only) ([fastmcp-pvl-core#318](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/fastmcp-pvl-core/pull/318), [#1465](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1465)). `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_S` makes the SIGTERM drain window configurable; its default of 3 seconds is the value 4.2 hardcoded ([fastmcp-pvl-core#331](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/fastmcp-pvl-core/pull/331), [#1550](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1550)).

### Logs

Logs are structured as `event_name key=value` and have one format switch, `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_LOG_FORMAT`: `rich` for a terminal, `json` for a collector. Unset, it picks Rich when stderr is a terminal and JSON everywhere else, so a container or journald now receives JSON with no configuration. `FASTMCP_ENABLE_RICH_LOGGING` is removed. `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_LOG_LEVEL` replaces `FASTMCP_LOG_LEVEL`; the old name still works through 5.x and logs a deprecation warning ([#1548](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1548), [#1550](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1550)). See [Configuration: logging](https://pvliesdonk.github.io/markdown-vault-mcp/unstable/reference/configuration/#logging).

### Startup

A configuration mistake stops the server with one `ERROR: configuration error: ...` line and exit code 1, including an event-store error under `--transport http` ([#1551](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1551), [#1570](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1570)). An explicit `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_AUTH_MODE` whose required settings are missing now refuses to start. In 4.2, three such configurations "started a server accepting unauthenticated connections": `oidc-proxy` without client credentials, `remote` without `BASE_URL`, and a whitespace-only bearer token ([fastmcp-pvl-core#338](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/fastmcp-pvl-core/pull/338)).

A vault directory that does not exist no longer crashes the server. It starts, logs `vault_directory_missing` at ERROR naming the variable, and every tool call fails until the directory is fixed; an unreadable directory logs `vault_directory_unreadable`. For the server process, an unset `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_SOURCE_DIR` now means `/data/vault` rather than a refusal to start. Managed git mode is exempt, since it clones into the directory ([#1590](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1590), [#1591](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1591), [#1646](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1646)).

## Links

### Links the server writes work in Obsidian

The OKF index generator, `okf_convert_links` and the link rewrite behind `rename` and `move_folder` wrote destinations with literal spaces. The indexer accepted them, but they are "invalid CommonMark links and fail in Obsidian" ([#1494](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1494), [#1514](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1514)). All three now write `%20`. They also escape the characters that would end or re-point a link: `#`, an unbalanced parenthesis, and brackets in a title. In 4.2, renaming a note to a name with an unbalanced `)` rewrote its links onto a shorter path, which pointed at a different note or at none ([#1516](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1516), [#1518](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1518)). Links already written with literal spaces are not repaired, and they are still read and indexed.

### The link graph holds more of what a reader follows

Backlinks, outlinks and broken-link reports come from the indexer's link extraction, which missed several valid CommonMark forms. It now reads:

- link text and reference labels containing an escaped `\]` ([#1520](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1520), [#1522](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1522));
- links whose text contains an unmatched or nested `[`, closing and opening at the nearest unmatched bracket ([#1529](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1529), [#1530](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1530));
- shortcut references, a bare `[label]` with a matching definition ([#1531](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1531), [#1533](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1533)).

Across 97,655 bracket arrangements, disagreements with the markdown-it-py reference parser went from 462 to 0 in the narrow set and from 5,574 to 0 in the wide one ([#1533](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1533)). One row goes away on purpose: `![alt][r]` whose definition points at a note is an image, and no longer counts as a link.

`rename` now rewrites the same links the index holds. In 4.2, a link like `[Bra\]cket](old.md)` was left pointing at the old name while the rename "still reports `updated_links=1`" ([#1521](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1521), [#1527](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1527)). A source the rewrite cannot change is no longer counted.

A file of unbalanced brackets could stall indexing: "A single such file stalls indexing for the whole vault" ([#1343](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1343)). Wikilinks are now matched with a linear scan; 40,000 `[` characters took about 29 s and now take 40 ms ([#1524](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1524)).

These changes alter what the index stores, so the first start after upgrading rebuilds the text index once, automatically.

## Large vaults and git-backed vaults

### Reindexing no longer scans the whole table per note

[@humblesuperintelligence](https://github.com/humblesuperintelligence) reported the cost on a vault of 25,380 notes: "every note that is added, modified, or reindexed pays one full-table scan", so a batch of changed notes costs time proportional to their number times the table size. A live incident "measured **1,526 GB read at up to 554 MB/s over 85 minutes**" ([#1535](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1535)). Three changes address it:

- Removing a note's search rows goes by row ID instead of scanning the content table. Existing databases are migrated once, in SQL, on first open ([#1539](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1539)).
- A reindex pass checkpoints its progress every 30 seconds, so an interrupted pass resumes rather than starting over ([#1540](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1540)).
- `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_BOOT_REINDEX=false` skips the reindex that reconciles offline changes at startup. It defaults to `true`, the 4.2 behaviour. With it off, edits made while no server was running stay invisible until a reindex runs, through the `reindex` tool or `markdown-vault-mcp reindex` ([#1543](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1543)).

Tuning SQLite's cache and memory map, also requested in #1535, was measured and not adopted; the maintainer found cache tuning "is counterproductive under exactly the memory pressure it was requested for" ([#1535 closing comment](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1535#issuecomment-5744048724)).

### The index follows git HEAD

In 4.2, a commit that deleted notes could reach the working tree through a path that did not reindex. `list_documents`, `list_folders` and `get_broken_links` then kept serving the deleted notes while `read` reported them gone ([#1532](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1532)). The server now records the HEAD the index last reflected and reindexes whenever the current HEAD differs, after every periodic pull, webhook delivery and `git_sync`. Its own commits cost no extra scan ([#1560](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1560)).

### Link tools wait for recent writes

`okf_convert_links` could skip a wikilink whose target had been written seconds earlier, because the index had not caught up ([#1464](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1464)). `okf_convert_links`, `okf_generate_index`, `rename` with `update_links` and `move_folder` now wait up to 60 seconds for queued index updates before touching files, and stop without changing anything if the refresh fails ([#1482](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1482)). See [index freshness after writes](https://pvliesdonk.github.io/markdown-vault-mcp/unstable/reference/tools/writer/index.md).

## OKF

### A bearer credential is not a person

In 4.2, writes made with a static bearer token were stamped `by: human:bearer-anon` in OKF provenance, while git attributed the same writes to the configured agent identity ([#1463](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1463)). Static bearer, mapped bearer and client-ID-only callers are now service principals: their writes stamp the server tool actor, and `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_OKF_VERIFY=trust-auth` refuses them for `okf_verify`. Review clients on bearer authentication should use `elicit`, the default, and show the confirmation to a person; an affirmative reply is recorded as `human:local`. Existing stamps are not rewritten. OAuth tokens that carry a `sub` claim keep their current attribution, pending [#1480](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1480) ([#1481](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1481)). The [OKF guide](https://pvliesdonk.github.io/markdown-vault-mcp/unstable/use/okf/#recording-a-human-review) covers each authentication case.

### Generated listings stay current

With `OKF_WRITE` on, `delete`, `rename` and `move_folder` left a folder's generated `index.md` listing notes that no longer existed, so `get_broken_links` reported the server's own entries ([#1609](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1609)). They now refresh every listing they make stale. `okf_generate_index` also wrote pointers to subfolder `index.md` files that did not exist ([#1647](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1647)); it now creates them, and reports them in a new `created` list ([#1648](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1648)). One visible effect: on an `OKF_WRITE` vault, the first refresh of an indexed folder creates `index.md` in every folder beneath it that lacks one, and on a git-backed vault those files land in commits.

## The Python library

The public import surface did not change, but four construction and exception contracts did.

**`Vault` takes `VaultSettings`.** The 31 configuration keywords deprecated in 4.2 are removed, along with both import paths for `to_vault_kwargs`. Passing an old keyword raises `TypeError` ([#1225](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1225), [#1478](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1478)):

```
from markdown_vault_mcp.vault import Vault, VaultSettings

vault = Vault(
    source_dir=root,
    settings=VaultSettings(read_only=False, index_path=index),
)
```

`source_dir` and the collaborators `embedding_provider`, `summarizer`, `git_strategy`, `on_write` and `chunk_strategy` stay keywords. Code building from `ProjectConfig` calls `to_vault_instances(config)`, then `to_vault_settings(config, instances=instances)`, then `Vault`; see the [configuration migration](https://pvliesdonk.github.io/markdown-vault-mcp/unstable/reference/api/config/#migrating-from-4x) and the [Vault migration](https://pvliesdonk.github.io/markdown-vault-mcp/unstable/reference/api/vault/#migrating-from-4x).

**Git strategies.** `GitWriteStrategy` drops `commit_name_claim` and `commit_email_claim`, and takes `git_lfs` and `repo_path` by keyword only; operators keep the `MARKDOWN_VAULT_MCP_GIT_COMMIT_*_CLAIM` variables ([#1236](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/issues/1236), [#1479](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1479)). The startup warning about a missing `git config user.email` is gone with them. A custom `git_strategy` must also provide `set_commit_observer`, and its `start()` receives an `on_tick` callback, both part of the `Syncer` protocol in `markdown_vault_mcp.git.interfaces` ([#1560](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1560)). See the [Git API migration](https://pvliesdonk.github.io/markdown-vault-mcp/unstable/reference/api/git/#migrating-from-4x).

**Exceptions.** A new `InvalidRequestError`, a `ValueError`, marks every refusal the caller caused; `DocumentNotFoundError`, `EmbeddingsNotConfiguredError` and the new `NoteTooLargeError` derive from it ([#1628](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1628)). Code that caught `ValueError` keeps working, and an `except ValueError` around a write now also catches a missing note. Two changes need code:

- `read()` returns `None` only when no file exists. A note that exists but cannot be read raises `DocumentUnreadableError`, which is not a `ValueError`. `read_revision()` raises it too, for invalid UTF-8 and Git LFS pointers ([#1627](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1627), [#1635](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1635)).
- `get_similar` raises `EmbeddingsNotConfiguredError` without embeddings, and `list_tags` raises on a field that is not indexed, instead of returning `[]` ([#1652](https://github.com/pvliesdonk/markdown-vault-mcp/pull/1652)).

`summarize`'s `notes_omitted` changes meaning as described [above](#how-a-tool-call-ends). The [exceptions reference](https://pvliesdonk.github.io/markdown-vault-mcp/unstable/reference/api/exceptions/index.md) lists the classes.
# Contribute

# Contribute

These pages are for whoever changes the project, including the agent working on a contributor's behalf. The rules for issues and pull requests, and where a fix belongs, are in `CONTRIBUTING.md`; `AGENTS.md` carries the conventions and the gates every pull request passes; the skills under `.agents/skills/` carry the task procedures. `SECURITY.md` says how to report a vulnerability privately, and the [security model](https://pvliesdonk.github.io/markdown-vault-mcp/unstable/security-model/index.md) is the page such a report argues against.

## Local development

The pull-request gate, the same commands CI runs:

```
uv sync --all-extras --all-groups                    # dev and docs tooling
uv run pre-commit install                            # hooks, once per clone
uv run pytest -x -q                                  # tests
uv run ruff check --fix . && uv run ruff format .    # lint and format
uv run mypy src/ tests/                              # type-check
```

CI runs the tests on Python 3.11 through 3.14; 3.14 also collects branch coverage and enforces the 80% total and patch coverage thresholds. To reproduce that run: `uv run --python 3.14 pytest --cov --cov-report=xml --durations=20`.

### Moving a clone

`uv sync` writes `.venv/bin/*` scripts with absolute shebangs. After moving the repository, `uv run pytest` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fastmcp'`. Recreate the environment:

```
rm -rf .venv
uv sync --all-extras --all-groups
```

### `uv.lock` after a template update

When a template update adds a dependency, the `uv sync --locked` step in CI fails against the stale lockfile. Run `uv lock` and commit the refreshed `uv.lock` with the update. CI never rewrites `uv.lock` in its own workspace, so lockfile drift shows as a red install step with a clear message.

## After scaffolding

Once, after `copier copy` and `gh repo create --push`:

1. Fill in the `DOMAIN-*` blocks in `README.md` and `AGENTS.md`. The `GENERATED-*` regions are not yours: the generators own them and rewrite them on every run.
1. Configure the GitHub secrets below.
1. Install the tooling and the hooks (the first two commands above).
1. Run the gate; push the first commit. CI should be green.

## GitHub secrets

The workflows read two required repository secrets and one optional token. Configure them under **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**, or with `gh secret set`:

| Secret                    | Used by                                                                                    | How to generate                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RELEASE_TOKEN`           | `release-prepare.yml`, `release.yml`, `copier-update.yml`, `renovate.yml`, `bootstrap.yml` | A fine-grained personal access token from <https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens/new> with `contents: write`, `pull_requests: write` and `administration: write` (bootstrap applies the repository rulesets, auto-merge, the security settings and the About block). It must belong to a repository admin: the shipped rulesets grant bypass to the admin role, and the tag and GitHub release that knope creates after a release pull request merges rely on it. Scoped to this repository. |
| `SONAR_TOKEN`             | `ci.yml`                                                                                   | <https://sonarcloud.io>: after importing the repository, open **Administration → Analysis Method**. Turn Automatic Analysis off first, because SonarQube Cloud refuses a CI scan while it is on; choosing GitHub Actions then shows the token. Until the secret exists, CI skips the scan.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` | `claude.yml`                                                                               | Optional. Run `claude setup-token` locally; configure it only for `@claude` or opted-in automatic review.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

```
gh secret set RELEASE_TOKEN
gh secret set SONAR_TOKEN
# Optional: enables @claude and opted-in automatic review.
gh secret set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN
```

`GITHUB_TOKEN` is provided by GitHub; nothing to configure. Dependency updates come from Renovate (`renovate.yml`), which reuses `RELEASE_TOKEN`, maintains `uv.lock` and merges patch and minor bumps once `CI Success` is green. `bootstrap.yml` enables auto-merge, applies the rulesets under `.github/rulesets/`, turns on private vulnerability reporting and Dependabot alerts, and fills the repository's About block from `pyproject.toml` on the first push; [repository protection](https://pvliesdonk.github.io/markdown-vault-mcp/unstable/contribute/repository-protection/index.md) has the per-branch posture. GitHub Actions versions are updated in the template and arrive through template updates, not per repository.
